queue.title: Close Dates Nobody Maintains Are Forecasts Nobody Should Trust
queue.brief: A close date that was set at deal creation and never touched again is worse than no close date at all — it creates false confidence. This post explains what maintaining close dates actually requires and how to build that habit into monday.com.
queue.description: H2s: 'What a Close Date Is Actually Supposed to Mean', 'The Quiet Way Bad Close Dates Wreck Your Forecast', 'How to Spot Dates That Have Never Been Touched', 'What a Meaningful Close Date Update Looks Like', 'Building a Weekly Habit Around Close Date Review'. Target keyword: monday.com close date accuracy. Concrete example: a rep whose five deals all show close dates from the first week of the quarter — none updated since — and what that makes the forecast look like when the manager pulls it on day 45.

queue.title: The Minimum CRM Routine a 5-Person Team Can Actually Sustain
queue.brief: Small sales teams can't afford a dedicated ops function, so CRM hygiene either gets baked into existing habits or it doesn't happen at all. This post gives a minimum viable routine that keeps monday.com usable without adding admin overhead.
queue.description: H2s: 'What to Track When You Have No Ops Person', 'The Three Fields That Matter Most on a Small Team', 'The 10-Minute Friday Check That Catches 80% of Problems', 'What You Can Safely Ignore Until You're Bigger', 'How to Split Manager vs Rep Responsibilities Without Formalising It'. Target keyword: monday.com CRM for small sales teams. Concrete example: a five-person team that runs a single 10-minute end-of-week board review using three filters — owner, last activity, and deal value — and how that habit keeps the pipeline clean enough to trust.
